paper.title: Learning Probably Approximately Correct Maximin Strategies in Simulation-Based Games with Infinite Strategy Spaces

settings.name_in_paper: Simulation-based two-player zero-sum game with finite strategy spaces, fixed-confidence maximin identification
unmapped: Arms are the n*m strategy profiles (x,y); goal is to identify the maximin profile (max over x of min over y of u(x,y)), not the best arm
Utility function u drawn from a GP prior with kernel k(pi,pi) <= 1, correlating arms
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the simulator is given a strategy profile $\boldsymbol{\pi}_t \in \Pi$ and returns an estimated utility $\tilde{u}_t \coloneqq u(\boldsymbol{\pi}_t) + e_t$, where $e_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \lambda)$ is i.i.d.~Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: Simulation-based two-player zero-sum game with finite strategy spaces, fixed-budget maximin identification
unmapped: Arms are the n*m strategy profiles; goal is to identify the maximin profile
Utility function drawn from a GP prior
settings.definition_quote: In the fixed-budget setting, the goal is to design $\delta$-PAC algorithms that, given the maximum number of available rounds $T$ (\emph{i.e.}, the budget), find an $\epsilon$-maximin strategy with confidence $1 - \delta_T$ as large as possible.

settings.name_in_paper: Simulation-based two-player zero-sum game with infinite strategy spaces (GP utility), fixed-confidence
unmapped: Strategy spaces X, Y are closed intervals in [0,1]; goal is to identify an epsilon-maximin strategy
Kernel smoothness assumption: GP sample derivatives exceed L with probability at most a exp(-L^2/b^2)
The learner knows the smoothness constants a, b (used to set grid size K_eps)
settings.definition_quote: A \emph{two-player zero-sum game with infinite strategy spaces} is a tuple $\Gamma = (\X, \Y, u)$, where $\X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $\Y \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ are compact and convex sets of strategies ... we model the utility as a sample from a GP

settings.name_in_paper: Simulation-based two-player zero-sum game with infinite strategy spaces (GP utility), fixed-budget
unmapped: Strategy spaces are closed intervals in [0,1]; goal is to identify an epsilon-maximin strategy
Kernel smoothness assumption with constants a, b
The learner knows the smoothness constants a, b (used to set grid size K_eps)
settings.definition_quote: An alternative is to consider the \emph{fixed-budget} case, where the maximum number of rounds $T$ is given in advance, and the goal is to minimize the probability $\delta$ that $\bar{x}$ is not an $\epsilon$-maximin strategy

source.label: thm:fixed_confidence
source.quote: Using a generic nondecreasing exploration term $b_t > 0$, the M-GP-LUCB algorithm stops its execution after at most $T_\delta$ rounds ... Specifically, letting $b_t := 2 \log \left( \frac{n\, m\, \pi^2\, t^2}{6 \delta} \right)$, the algorithm returns a maximin profile with confidence at least $1 - \delta$, and: T_\delta \leq 64 \,H^*(u)\, \lambda ( \log ( 64 H^*(u) \lambda \pi \sqrt{\frac{n m}{6 \delta}} ) + 2 \log ( \log ( ... ) ) )

results.notes: Correctness w.p. >= 1-delta and stopping bound holds on the good event. The theorem also gives a generic bound T_delta <= inf{t: 8 H* b_t lambda - lambda n m/sigma^2 < t} for any nondecreasing b_t, not recorded separately. Probability is over GP prior and noise.

symbols.lambda_n: variance of the Gaussian simulator noise
symbols.H_2: max_i i * Delta_(i)^{-2}, Delta_(i) = |u(pi*) - u(pi_i)| sorted

conditions: u drawn from GP(0,k) with k(pi,pi) <= 1

source.label: thm:fixed_budget
source.quote: Letting $T$ be the number of available rounds, the GP-SE algorithm returns a maximin strategy profile $\bpi^\ast$ with confidence at least $1 - \delta_T$, where: \delta_T \coloneqq 2 P (n + m - 2) e^{-\frac{T - P}{8 \lambda \overline{\log}(P) H_2}}, and $H_2 \coloneqq \max_{i \in \{1, \ldots, P\}} i \, \Delta_{(i)}^{-2}$.

bound.expression_latex: T_{\delta, \epsilon} \leq 64 \, H^*(u) \, \lambda \left[ \log \left( 64 \, H^*(u)\, \lambda \, \pi \, K_\epsilon \, \sqrt{\frac{1}{3 \delta}} \right) + 2 \, \log \left( \log \left( 64 \, H^*(u) \lambda \, \pi \, K_\epsilon \sqrt{\frac{1}{3 \delta}} \right) \right) \right]
